subject.title: fix: recover stranded replies in message_tool_only mode (#85714)

question: Should OpenClaw accept a default-off `messages.strandedReplyRecovery` option that re-prompts the model with normalized private `message_tool_only` final text to deliver via `message(action=send)`?
rationale: The code path is reviewable, but automation cannot choose the product and privacy contract for opt-in recovery of private final text across channels, especially with #99536 proposing a different default policy.

options.title: Accept opt-in recovery after proof
options.body: Keep the default false, require redacted real external channel proof, and let operators opt into one-shot recovery when they prefer recovery over strict silence.

options.title: Keep strict tool-only semantics
options.body: Reject the recovery surface and rely on stronger prompts, stronger models, or `automatic` visible replies for operators who cannot tolerate silence.

options.title: Choose a different recovery policy
options.body: Pause this branch and use #99536 or the canonical issue to settle a default-on or diagnostic-only policy instead.

recommendation.title: Accept opt-in recovery after proof
recommendation.body: Keep the default false, require redacted real external channel proof, and let operators opt into one-shot recovery when they prefer recovery over strict silence.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision sits on the core source-reply privacy boundary and the recent merged warning-only work carries a steipete rewrite signal.
